data.narrative:
Monumo is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Martin Frost, Ian Murphy, and Dominic Vergine, with $100M total raised to date. The valuation analysis applies two triangulation methods against a comp universe of 8 private peers (including SambaNova Systems, Etched, d-Matrix, Positron AI, and DEEPX) and 3 public semiconductor anchors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD).

The Stage-Progression method, applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier to the $100M raised proxy, implies a valuation of $190M. The Peer-Median approach across five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $2.0B median, with a range spanning $529M (DEEPX) to $11.0B (SambaNova). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (21.4x median across the three public semiconductors) is not applicable absent disclosed revenue. 

Triangulating these two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $162M to $2.3B, with a median of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty in peer comparability—particularly the stage and magnitude variance within the private comp set—and the absence of revenue visibility typical in early-stage semiconductor ventures. The Stage-Progression floor suggests downside protection from capital deployed; the Peer-Median ceiling is anchored to late-stage frontier-chip companies commanding elevated valuations. Resolution of business traction and competitive positioning against the sample peer set would materially narrow this range.
